title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 31-32
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 31 to 32 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुः शशबिन्दुः सुरेश्वरः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 31 to 32 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 31 to 32.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 31 to 32** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुः शशबिन्दुः सुरेश्वरः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुः शशबिन्दुः सुरेश्वरः । औषधं जगतः सेतुः सत्यधर्मपराक्रमः ॥** **भूतभव्यभवन्नाथः पवनः पावनोऽनलः । कामहा कामकृत्कान्तः कामः कामप्रदः प्रभुः ॥**

He rises as the Moon and shines as the Sun. The Lord of the gods is that God of gods. He is the medicine and the bridge that carries the world across; truth and dharma are his strength. He is the lord of what was and what will be, the wind and the purifying fire. The one who fulfils desires and ends them is that God of gods. Lovable, love itself, the Lord who gives what we ask.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 31 to 32 mean?
faq.a: He rises as the Moon and shines as the Sun. The Lord of the gods is that God of gods. He is the medicine and the bridge that carries the world across; truth and dharma are his strength. He is the lord of what was and what will be, the wind and the purifying fire. The one who fulfils desires and ends them is that God of gods. Lovable, love itself, the Lord who gives what we ask.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
